# GoalBuddy coding instructions

GoalBuddy helps students, professionals, and individuals turn goals into milestones and tasks, then track task-based progress. Preserve the Week 02 specification and constitution. Week 03 implements a public shell and explicitly labeled empty-workspace previews; authentication, saved goal workflows, and AI are not implemented.

Use the installed Next.js 16.4.6 App Router, React 19.3.0, strict TypeScript, Tailwind 4.3.3, ESLint, Prettier, Node.js and npm lockfile. Read relevant `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` guides before coding; this version's route error boundary uses `retry`. PostgreSQL/Supabase, Auth.js/Clerk, Vercel, and AI providers remain provisional. Do not invent credentials, add unnecessary dependencies, or claim a connected backend.

`app/layout.tsx` composes the shared header, main landmark and footer. `app/page.tsx` is the public homepage; `app/(workspace)/` contains the preview routes and disclosure. Reuse `components/layout/`, `components/ui/` and `components/dashboard-summary.tsx`. Domain types live in `lib/models.ts`; design and future boundaries live in `specs/001-goalbuddy/plan.md` and `data-model.md`. Add future server-only auth/data modules under `lib/server/`, validation under `lib/validation/`, and route handlers under `app/api/` according to the existing specification. Do not create empty placeholder modules.

Prefer Server Components. Add Client Components only for interaction or browser APIs. Never import server credentials or data access into client components. Use explicit props, type-only imports, discriminated unions when useful, no application `any`, no code/configuration/HTML comments, and no unrelated refactoring. Follow existing Prettier settings. Use shared abstractions only for concrete reuse.

Use Tailwind utilities and tokens from `app/globals.css`. Keep semantic headings, labels, keyboard controls, visible focus, reduced-motion support, and 320/768/1280px plus 200% zoom usability. Preserve the system font stack for network-independent builds. Follow `docs/design-system.md`. Never misrepresent a preview as a working saved feature.

P1 entities are User, Goal, Milestone, Task with server-issued IDs, positive revisions and UTC timestamps. Goals have one immutable owner; milestones belong to one goal; tasks belong to a goal and optionally a milestone of that same goal. Dates are optional date-only strings. Completion sets a timestamp; reopening clears it. Progress is derived from tasks, zero for no tasks and rounded otherwise. Count milestone tasks once; account progress is task-weighted. No ProgressEntry table or manually editable percentage is approved.

Future authentication must use a documented provider decision and verified server identity. Enforce ownership on every read and write, including nested parents; never trust client owner IDs. Unauthorized collections must not return data; missing and foreign resources have indistinguishable 404 responses. No shared caching of private data; private HTTP responses use no-store. Use secure session cookies and CSRF protection where applicable. Never expose tokens, credentials, personal goal text, or AI prompts in logs or source.

Validate all untrusted input server-side with field allowlists, the specification's lengths, valid dates/timezones, boolean completion, 64 KiB JSON body limit, and safe HTTP errors. Shared TypeScript types are not runtime validation. Use atomic transactions, revision conflict checks, deadline consistency, cascade deletion confirmation, and per-goal locking as designed. Preserve entered values on recoverable failures; do not report unsaved changes as successful.

Before review run `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `npm run build`. Use `.cmd` launchers on Windows when PowerShell blocks scripts. No test runner is configured yet. Add meaningful workflow/security tests with persistence: two users, foreign/mismatched parents, rollback, stale revisions, date boundaries, completion/reopen, 0-task and 2/3 progress cases. Report actual browser, accessibility and test limits rather than asserting they passed.

Reuse existing GitHub issues #3–#17 and their acceptance criteria; do not duplicate them. Use feature branches, user-selected commit messages, PRs and a real approving review before merging main. Week 03 preserves unmerged Week 02 ancestry; disclose this exception. Do not commit, push, create PRs or merge without the user's applicable authorization. Independently completed work must never be attributed to inactive teammates or invented meetings/reviews.

Prioritize P1 identity, ownership, goal/milestone/task CRUD and basic progress. P2 adds organization/enhanced dashboard. P3 AI is optional and never blocks manual planning; generated content must be separately reviewed and validated before explicit acceptance. No notifications, social sharing, payments or expanded scope without a new justified requirement.
